column1: # What a comparison returns. Registering this kind is what turns
# `1000 ميغابايت = 1 غيغابايت` from an unresolvable expression into `true`.
# `true` and `false` are not translated, and that is this file's finding
# rather than an oversight it hides: the kind ships no vocabulary at all,
# so `formatValue` degrades to the unit key in every language. An Arabic
# engine answering "true" is what the code does today, and a row asserting
# it is what makes a later `boolean/locale/ar` a visible diff here.
# Every numeral below is Latin. Arabic-Indic digits do not read — they are
# dropped rather than refused, and the quantity silently defaults to 1 — so
# a row written with them would record a wrong answer that looks right.
# The six plural categories, read rather than written: 0 zero, 1 one, 2 two,
# 3-10 few, 11-99 many, else other. Only Arabic types six different words
# `أمتار` above and `أقدام` below are broken plurals: the stem is rewritten
# rather than suffixed, which is why a `few` form cannot be derived from
# the singular the way an -s or an -ów could.
# Latin digits with a comma group and a dot decimal, inside a right-to-left
# sentence — the English pair, in the one language that reads the other way.
# `في` is both "in" and "times", and it is claimed for the conversion, so
# `ضرب` is what multiplication is left with.
# Division is two tokens: the noun `قسمة` and `على` as `keywords.by`.
